specs.anchorText: A corner is localizable in both dimensions, and that is the whole reason this chapter hunts for corners rather than edges.
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette: three cartoon characters playing hide-and-seek behind a small viewing window. On the left, a blank-faced character on a plain wall is impossible to find because everywhere looks identical (shrugging seeker surrounded by question marks). In the middle, a character standing on a long straight stripe can only be pinned down across the stripe but slides freely along it (shown sliding sideways on a rail). On the right, a confident character sitting exactly at the inside corner where two walls meet is instantly found and pointed at by a happy seeker. White background. The style should be friendly and approachable, like a comic strip or an XKCD-inspired infographic, expressive characters, minimal clutter, suitable for a technical textbook. No text or lettering in the image. Gentle, immediately understandable humor. One clear visual metaphor: corners are the only places you can locate something again.
specs.alt: Three hide-and-seek scenes: a seeker baffled by a blank wall, a character sliding along a stripe so only one direction is pinned down, and a character caught instantly at a corner where two walls meet, dramatizing why corners are findable while flat regions and edges are not.
specs.caption: On a blank wall you are everywhere; on an edge you can still slide; only at a corner are you pinned down in both directions, which is why corners are the points worth detecting.

specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette: a tug-of-war over a long flexible measuring tape that represents a fitted line. On the left version, a single oversized mischievous outlier character with a grin yanks the tape sharply off course while a crowd of small honest dot-characters strain helplessly the other way, the tape bent toward the liar (least squares, fooled). On the right version, the same crowd of honest dots stand calmly along a straight tape inside a soft tolerance band while the few liar characters are politely fenced off to the side with an OUT gate, the line straight and true (RANSAC, robust). White background. The style should be friendly and approachable, like a comic strip or an XKCD-inspired infographic, expressive characters, minimal clutter, suitable for a technical textbook. No text or lettering in the image. Gentle humor. One clear visual metaphor: one loud liar drags the naive fit, while the robust fit fences the liars out and trusts the honest majority.
specs.alt: A tug-of-war on a flexible measuring tape: on one side a single huge outlier yanks the fitted line off course while honest dots strain helplessly, on the other the robust fit keeps the line straight inside a tolerance band and fences the few liars out a gate, contrasting least squares with RANSAC.
specs.caption: Least squares lets one loud liar drag the whole fit off true; RANSAC trusts the consensus of the honest and fences the outliers out, handing back a verdict on every point.
